newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka sees 1997 gas oil imports at 690,950 t.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka sees 1997 gas oil imports at 690,950 t.

text.p: Sri Lankan state oil company Ceylon Petroleum Corp (CPC) said on Wednesday it expects to import 690,950 tonnes of gas oil this year, up around 100,000 tonnes from 1996.

CPC Chairman Anil Obeyesekere told Reuters in an interview that the company had so far bought 530,450 tonnes of gas oil in 1997 and expected to take in another 160,500 tonnes for the balance of the year.
Actual imports in 1996 totalled 592,450 tonnes, he said.
He said 1998 gas oil imports were likely to be around 720,000 tonnes.
CPC buys gas oil in regular cargo-sized lots by tender from the international spot market.

The increase in gas oil imports in 1997 was due mainly to a 45-day maintenance shutdown at CPC's 50,000-60,000 barrels per day oil refinery at Sapugaskanda, north of the capital Colombo, between January and March.
The refinery normally produces between 1,000 and 1,300 tonnes of gas oil a day and the turnaround left a large gap in supply which had to be filled with imports, he said.
But he said the Indian Ocean island's gas oil consumption was also growing steadily due to increasing demand from oil-fired power stations and from the transportation sector.
"Estimates are that there is a 10-15 percent growth rate (per year) in the consumption of diesel due to thermal power and due to the increased transport activity," he said.
Obeyesekere said total Sri Lankan gas oil demand would increase by around 50 percent over the next three to four years:
"Say we imported around 590,000 tonnes in 1996, so it should be say about 50 percent more by the end of the year 2000."
